newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S BANK HANDLOWY IPO SEEN IN JUNE - OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S BANK HANDLOWY IPO SEEN IN JUNE - OFFICIAL.

text.p: Poland's largest commercial bank, Bank Handlowy SA, plans to hold its initial public offering for 30 percent of shares in June, a deputy finance minister said on Wednesday.
"There will be a public offering of Bank Handlowy in June. That's our plan," Ryszard Pazura told Reuters.
The government plans to sell 30 percent of Handlowy's shares in a public offering and later in 1997 offer another 30 percent stake to an institutional investor.
A further 30-percent-stake will be earmarked for pension funds after the country carries out its social security reform.

The remaining shares will be divided between a planned fund to meet claims for property taken under communism and bank employees. The finance ministry said it expected to earn about 900 million zlotys by the Handlowy sale.
Handlowy had a net profit of 390.3 million zlotys in the first six months of 1996. Its balance sheet total amounted to 10.46 billion zlotys in the first half of 1996.

Pazura also said earlier plans of selling a Handlowy stake to an institutional investor first and carrying out a public offering in the second half of the year were changed because Poland wanted to sell another large bank at the same time.

The finance ministry earlier said a 15-percent public offer of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) will take place in September, after it finds an investor or a group of investors to take 65 percent of the bank.
HSBC, the ministry's adviser in selling PBK, said last year that the bank was worth between 1.2 and 1.6 billion zlotys.
PBK's balance sheet total amounted to 8.4 billion zlotys after nine months of 1996.
